title: Staggered readiness backoff and traffic contract enforcement for SLO preservation
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Problem: During multi-region failovers and heavy-tail traffic bursts, readiness probes oscillate and cause autoscaler thrash leading to elevated p99 latency and SLO violations. Goal: Implement a staged readiness backoff model combined with token-weighted traffic contracts and a scale-back controller to stabilize autoscaling decisions, preserve SLOs, and provide predictable failover behavior.

Scope: design + simulation harness + controller changes + edge admission changes + runbook updates. This ticket coordinates SRE, Serving Runtime, and Edge teams to land the feature behind a feature flag and roll it out gradually.
acceptance_criteria: Simulated multi-region failover scenario shows <10% additional p99 latency vs baseline and no autoscaler thrash in a 30-minute window
End-to-end synthetic spike test reduces scale events by >=60% compared to current baseline with identical arrival patterns
Edge token-weighted admission enforces traffic contracts and drops/degrades low-priority tokens first under constrained conditions
Runbook updated with play-by-play failover steps, rollback plan, and operator checks; runbook validated in a tabletop exercise
All code changes merged and e2e smoke tests pass in staging and dedicated clusters under feature flag
implementation_notes: Introduce a readiness_state finite state machine: OK -> SOFT_DEGRADED -> HARD_DEGRADED. Map probe outcomes to these states with configurable hysteresis windows.
Probe smoothing: apply an EWMA (alpha=0.12) over a 30s window to readiness signals to reduce sensitivity to transient spikes.
Staged backoff timers: configurable triage windows (soft: 10s, medium: 60s, hard: 5m) applied per-region. Promote/demote using a quorum heuristic to avoid ripple effects.
Scale-back controller: defer scale-downs for up to 2x the observed scale-up window unless memory/cpu headroom confirms steady-state. Add a cooldown metric to prevent thrash.
Traffic contracts at ingress: token-weighted admission where tokens carry a priority label; admission controller enforces per-priority drop policies under memory/latency pressure.
Instrumentation: add metrics for readiness_state_transitions, smoothing_outlier_count, scale_event_count, token_drop_by_priority, and scale_back_cooldown_seconds.
Rollout plan: feature-flagged -> staging -> EU-west canary (10% traffic for 48h) -> ramp to 20% -> global depending on metrics.
Backward compatibility: default behavior preserved until feature flag enabled on per-cluster basis. Safe fallback clears side-effects (token policy disabled, controller no-op).
progress_updates: 2026-01-29: Kickoff with SRE, Runtime, Edge, and PM. Agreed on staged-state model and token-weighted admission approach.
2026-02-05: Simulation harness implemented (github.com/redwood-inference/sim PR-112). Early sims show ~40% fewer scale cycles but p99 remains elevated in heavy-tail mixes.
2026-02-18: Tuned EWMA alpha and smoothing window after reviewing incident-2025-11-04 traces; switched alpha from 0.2 -> 0.12 which reduced probe churn in sims.
2026-02-28: Security design review: token priority header must be signed. Decided to HMAC tokens with KMS-backed keys. Security PR created (PR-3245).
2026-03-04: Prototype staged backoff controller implemented in controller repo (PR-5471). Canary deployed to staging cluster behind feature flag.
2026-03-09: Staging canary results: scale events reduced by 65% over 1h burn-in; observed higher 95th latency on long-running batch jobs — investigating per-route admission buffers.
review_comments: Evan Brooks (SRE): 'Quorum-based promotion preferred over simple timers to avoid noisy-region promotions; recommend 2-of-3 regional agreement before HARD_DEGRADED.'
Liam Chen (Runtime): 'KV cache pressure interacts with readiness state transitions. Consider a memory short-circuit to HARD_DEGRADED when memory > 92% to avoid OOM thrash.'
Maya Gupta (Security): 'Token priority header must be HMAC-signed; KMS integration scope added. Ensure tokens are short-lived to reduce replay risk.'
Asha Patel (PM): 'Document rollback steps and customer impact expectations per rollback step. Tie alerts to SLO windows so on-call has clear thresholds.'
next_steps: Resolve increased 95th latency for batch jobs by adding per-route admission thresholds and a small buffer pool for batch tokens.
Complete security KMS PR and land token signing (PR-3245).
Add e2e smoke tests for canary region and add alerts for readiness_state churn and scale_back_cooldown violations.
Prepare canary rollout to EU-west with 10% traffic for 48h and run tabletop follow-up with on-call rotation.
